title: Blue Bounces!
suggestedTopics: Why do clouds look white and fluffy?
Why does the moon change shape every night?
Where do rainbows come from after the rain?

steps.title: Look up
steps.teachingGoal: Ask the one question the whole lesson answers.
steps.narration: Look up! The sky is blue. Where does the blue come from?
steps.concept: The sky looks blue everywhere, so something must make it that colour.
steps.summary: Tung asks where the blue of the sky comes from.
steps.visualAction: Wide low-angle shot: Tung stands in a grassy field and points straight up at a huge flat blue sky that fills the top of the frame.

steps.title: White light is a hiding place
steps.teachingGoal: Show that white sunlight is all the colours together.
steps.narration: Sunlight looks plain white. But every colour is hiding inside it.
steps.concept: White sunlight is all the colours mixed together.
steps.summary: Every colour hides inside plain white sunlight.
steps.visualAction: Medium shot on a dark background: one narrow white sunbeam cuts across the frame, and Tung leans in close to peer along it.

steps.title: The rainbow jumps out
steps.teachingGoal: Split white light into named colours the child already knows.
steps.narration: Let the light out, and a rainbow jumps free. Red, yellow, green, blue!
steps.concept: White light can be split into a rainbow of separate colours.
steps.summary: The white beam splits into a rainbow fan.
steps.visualAction: Snap cut to a close shot: the white beam strikes a clear glass block and springs out of the far side as a wide rainbow fan that sweeps across the frame.

steps.title: Bouncy blue, slow red
steps.teachingGoal: Give blue and red one physical character each.
steps.narration: Blue is the tiny bouncy colour. Red is the big slow one.
steps.concept: Blue light is small and bounces easily, and red light is big and travels straight.
steps.summary: Blue is small and bouncy, and red is big and slow.
steps.visualAction: Split frame: on the left a small blue ball bounces fast and high, on the right a big red ball rolls slowly in a straight line, and Tung looks from one side to the other.

steps.title: The air is not empty
steps.teachingGoal: Reveal the air as something the colours can hit.
steps.narration: The air looks empty. It is not! It is full of tiny bits.
steps.concept: Air is made of countless tiny bits that are too small to see.
steps.summary: Empty-looking air is full of tiny bits.
steps.visualAction: The camera pushes in slowly on plain blue air until countless pale specks drift into view, and Tung steps in beside them and taps one.

steps.title: Red goes straight through
steps.teachingGoal: Show red light passing the air bits without a bounce.
steps.narration: Big slow red goes straight past the tiny bits. Whoosh!
steps.concept: Red light travels through the air without being knocked off course.
steps.summary: Red light passes the tiny bits in a straight line.
steps.visualAction: Flat side-on diagram shot: a big red ball rolls through a drifting field of specks in one straight line and leaves the frame, while Tung tracks it with a sweeping point.

steps.title: Blue bounces
steps.teachingGoal: Show blue light scattering off the air bits.
steps.narration: Little blue hits them and bounces away. Boing! Boing!
steps.concept: Blue light hits the tiny bits of air and bounces off in new directions.
steps.summary: Blue light bounces off the tiny bits of air.
steps.visualAction: The same side-on diagram: a small blue ball enters, strikes speck after speck, and ricochets in a new direction on every hit, with a snappy held pose at each bounce.

steps.title: The whole sky fills up
steps.teachingGoal: Turn one bounce into a sky full of blue, with a refrain.
steps.narration: Blue bounces all over the sky. Say it with me: blue bounces!
steps.concept: Bounced blue light spreads out until it fills the whole sky.
steps.summary: Bounced blue light fills the whole sky.
steps.visualAction: Fast pull back to a wide shot: hundreds of blue balls ricochet across the sky until the frame turns solid blue, and Tung cheers from the bottom corner.

steps.title: Blue reaches you
steps.teachingGoal: Connect the scattered blue to what the child sees.
steps.narration: So blue comes down to your eyes from every part of the sky.
steps.concept: You see blue from every direction because bounced blue light arrives from everywhere.
steps.summary: Bounced blue light arrives from every direction.
steps.visualAction: Ground-level shot from behind Tung: thin blue arrows rain down from every part of the sky and meet at the spot where he stands looking up.

steps.title: Not the sea
steps.teachingGoal: Correct the common idea that the sky copies the ocean.
steps.narration: The sky is not blue because the sea is blue. Deserts have blue sky too!
steps.concept: The sky is not a reflection of the ocean.
steps.summary: The sky is blue over dry deserts as well as over the sea.
steps.visualAction: Hard wipe from a blue sea to a dry orange desert under the same blue sky, where Tung stands on the sand and shakes his head at a crossed-out wave symbol.

steps.title: Sunset red
steps.teachingGoal: Use the same rule to explain a sunset.
steps.narration: At sunset the light travels far. The blue bounces away, and red stays.
steps.concept: At sunset light crosses much more air, so the blue bounces away and red light is left.
steps.summary: Sunsets are red because the blue has bounced away.
steps.visualAction: Slow wide shot: the sun sinks, its long light path stretches across the frame, blue balls peel off to the sides, and the sky fades to orange and red around Tung.

steps.title: Blue bounces everywhere
steps.teachingGoal: Close on the one sentence the child should keep.
steps.narration: The sky is blue because blue bounces. Blue bounces everywhere!
steps.concept: Blue light bounces most in air, so the sky looks blue.
steps.summary: The sky is blue because blue light bounces most.
steps.visualAction: Back to the opening field: the camera tilts up from Tung to the full blue sky while a few blue balls bounce past the frame.
